matrix.label: Elective recovery funding envelope available to the ICB (18 months)
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Unsourced estimate — analyst judgement with no published source, or a quantity for which no public figure exists at any level.
matrix.evidence_basis: No ICB-level elective recovery budget is published at any level. The Phase 3 default of £15m was set as an illustrative, deliberately binding envelope, never as a sourced figure. Range spans half to double that anchor.

matrix.label: Diagnostic tests required to unlock one completed RTT pathway
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Unsourced estimate — analyst judgement with no published source, or a quantity for which no public figure exists at any level.
matrix.evidence_basis: The single remaining unsourced figure in the Phase 3 cost model, flagged as such throughout. No NHS dataset publishes this ratio. It sets the unit cost of the diagnostic lever and therefore how much capacity a given budget buys through it. The upper bound is set at 3.50 deliberately: the diagnostic and treatment levers are indifferent at 3.34 tests per pathway (see tipping_points()), and a range that stopped short of that point would conceal the only decision in the model rather than test it. Three or more tests to reach a treatment decision is clinically ordinary on complex pathways, so the bound is plausible as well as convenient.

matrix.label: Unit cost of elective activity relative to NCC 2024/25 baseline
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Sourced — published national dataset covering the current period (NCC 2024/25; NHS Payment Scheme 2025/26).
matrix.evidence_basis: Unit costs are sourced from NCC 2024/25 and the 2025/26 NHS Payment Scheme. Graded low-uncertainty on provenance, but ranged anyway: the removal of the ERF marginal-rate mechanism for 2025/26 is direct evidence that payment policy does change materially between years.

matrix.label: Over-52-week backlog to be cleared, relative to central forecast
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Measured — derived from this warehouse's own observed data with a quantified interval attached (Phase 2 Monte Carlo forecast).
matrix.evidence_basis: Taken directly from the Phase 2 Monte Carlo waiting-list forecast: the ratio of the p5 and p95 ICB totals to the p50 total at horizon end (September 2027). Measured, not assumed.

matrix.label: Independent-sector headroom above current NHS-funded activity
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Unsourced estimate — analyst judgement with no published source, or a quantity for which no public figure exists at any level.
matrix.evidence_basis: Analyst assumption from Phase 3, chosen on the reasoning that the independent sector is more scalable short-term than NHS in-house capacity. No published measure of independent-sector spare elective capacity for this ICB exists.

matrix.label: Achievable uplift in NHS in-house elective completions
matrix.evidence_grade_meaning: Anchored estimate — extrapolated from warehouse data or from a stated national policy target, but not itself a published figure.
matrix.evidence_basis: Anchored on the Elective Recovery Fund's own national 10% activity increase target plus a buffer. Policy-anchored, but the achievable rate for these specific trusts is not published.

strategies.name: Hold position
strategies.summary: Commit no additional recovery funding. The backlog follows its business-as-usual trajectory.
strategies.rationale: Included because a do-nothing baseline is the only way to state what the other strategies buy. In wayfinding terms this is the practical-coping trajectory the ICB is already on.
strategies.flex_note: Fully reversible — no commitment is made.
strategies.insure_note: No downside to insure against beyond the backlog itself.
strategies.institutional: High legitimacy risk. Regulator and public expectation is visible action on 52-week waits; inaction is not a defensible position even where it is affordable.

strategies.name: Unconstrained optimisation
strategies.summary: Allocate the full envelope wherever the model says it clears the most breaches, with the standing 15pp equity tolerance.
strategies.rationale: The Phase 3 answer, carried forward unchanged so that the value of every added constraint can be read off against it.
strategies.flex_note: Mixed. Scalability depends on which levers the optimum happens to select, which is not stable across scenarios.
strategies.insure_note: Hard to contract against, because the commitment is not describable in advance of the solve.
strategies.institutional: Moderate risk. An allocation that changes shape whenever an input is revised is difficult to defend to provider boards, who experience it as arbitrary.

strategies.name: NHS delivery only
strategies.summary: Deliver recovery entirely through NHS providers — in-house treatment capacity or diagnostic capacity. No independent-sector outsourcing.
strategies.rationale: Tests the position that recovery money should build durable NHS capability rather than buy activity that leaves no residue.
strategies.flex_note: Low. Substantive capacity implies recruitment and estate commitments that cannot be unwound within the horizon.
strategies.insure_note: Limited. Fixed costs persist if demand falls away.
strategies.institutional: High legitimacy within the provider field; aligns with professional and staff-side expectations about where recovery money should go.

strategies.name: No in-house expansion
strategies.summary: Deliver recovery by buying independent-sector activity and by unlocking diagnostics. No expansion of in-house treatment capacity.
strategies.rationale: Tests the opposite position: fastest access to activity, no long-term cost base.
strategies.flex_note: High. Contracted volumes can be scaled or stopped between periods.
strategies.insure_note: Good. Volume risk sits with the provider under a per-case contract.
strategies.institutional: Contested. Independent-sector reliance is politically sensitive within the NHS field and attracts staff-side objection even where it performs.

strategies.name: Diagnostic-led recovery
strategies.summary: Direct at least half the envelope to diagnostic capacity, on the basis that diagnostics gate the pathway.
strategies.rationale: Tests whether unlocking the diagnostic constraint clears more pathways per pound than adding treatment capacity directly.
strategies.flex_note: Moderate. Equipment and workforce commitments are partly reversible; capital elements are not.
strategies.insure_note: Weak. Benefit depends on the unsourced conversion ratio.
strategies.institutional: Strong legitimacy — matches the national diagnostic-capacity policy direction and is readily explained to boards.

strategies.name: Equity-first
strategies.summary: Require higher-deprivation providers to receive at least their baseline share of the breaches cleared. No equity tolerance.
strategies.rationale: Tests the cost of removing the 15pp tolerance and holding a hard proportionality floor instead.
strategies.flex_note: Moderate — the constraint binds allocation, not contract form.
strategies.institutional: Strong legitimacy. Directly answers the statutory duty to reduce inequalities in access and is straightforward to evidence.

strategies.name: Treatment capacity only
strategies.summary: Fund treatment capacity — in-house or independent sector — and nothing through the diagnostic lever.
strategies.rationale: The counterpart to S4, and the strategy that prices the diagnostic bet. Because the diagnostic lever rests entirely on the one unsourced parameter in the model, this shows what the programme delivers if that assumption is set aside altogether.
strategies.flex_note: Mixed — depends on the in-house / outsourced split, which is left to the solve.
strategies.institutional: Low risk but low ambition. Treats the diagnostic constraint as fixed, which sits awkwardly against national policy emphasis on diagnostic capacity.

strategies.name: Diversified hedge
strategies.summary: Cap any single lever at 50% of spend, so the programme is never more than half exposed to one delivery assumption.
strategies.rationale: Constructed against the Ch.8 principle that keeping options open beats optimising to a single expected case when the key inputs are weakly evidenced.
strategies.flex_note: Good. Any one strand can be scaled back without collapsing the programme.
strategies.insure_note: Moderate — the outsourced strand carries contractual protection, the others less so.
strategies.institutional: Defensible. Spreads exposure across the competing positions in the field rather than adjudicating between them.
